Deg. |Spironema fragrans|Lindl. }} }} '''''Callisia fragrans''''', the '''false bromeliad''', '''false bromeliad plant''' or '''golden tendril''', is a [[flowering plant]] species of the genus ''[[Callisia]]'', in the [[Commelinids|spiderwort]] family, [[Commelinaceae]] that is native to [[Mexico]].{{cite web|title=Plants database |url=https://plants.usda.gov/home/plantProfile?symbol=CAFR6|publisher=United States Department of Agriculture|access-date=9 February 2022}} ==Description== [[File:Starr-070525-7173-Callisia fragrans-flowering habit-Kula-Maui (24889399755).jpg|thumb|left|A flowering clump]] A robust, perennial [[herbaceous]] plant, the fleshy stem of ''Callisia fragrans'' can grow to a height of {{convert|1.5|m|ft|abbr=on}}. The leaves are {{convert|25|cm|in|abbr=on}} long and become burgundy-violet if exposed to more prolonged sunlight (an example of "sun-stressing"). Flowering shoots are [[bromeliad]]-like, vigorous, and covered with almost [[Rosette (botany)|rosette]]-like leaves. They are sparsely branched. Long, fairly slender, distichous [[stolon]]s emerge from the lower [[node (botany)|nodes]]. The leaves of flowering [[Shoot (botany)|shoots]] are up to 30 centimeters long and 7 centimeters wide. They are bright light green, narrowly elliptic-lanceolate, pointed, almost stem-clasping, and usually [[glabrous]]. ===Inflorescence === [[File:Callisia fragrans, bloeiwyse, Manie van der Schijff BT, a.jpg |thumb|left |245px |Close-up of the small flowers]] The almost sessile, small white flowers are fragrant, which occur from late winter to spring.[https://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Callisia~fragrans#:~:text=Inflorescences%20terminal%2C%20panicle%2Dlike%2C,3%2Dvalved%20capsules.&text=Flowering%3A%20Late%20Winter%20to%20Spring. Callisia fragrans (Lindl.) Woodson] by PlantNET. Retrieved 11 May, 2025. The spreading inflorescence consists of terminal [[panicle]]s with crowded branches. The [[sessile (botany)|sessile]], paired whorls are borne on papery [[bract]]s up to 2 centimeters long. heir bristly [[sepal]]s are 3.5 to 5 millimeters long and 1.5 to 2 millimeters wide. The lanceolate to ovate, white petals have no flat blade. They are 5 to 6 millimeters long and 2.5 to 3.5 millimeters wide. The six long, protruding, white [[stamen]]s are more conspicuous than the [[petal]]s. Their connectives are [[membranous]]. The [[Stigma (botany)|stigma]] is brush-shaped.{{cite book |title=Flowering Plants. Monocotyledons: Alismatanae and Commelinanae (except Gramineae) |page=89 |author=Klaus Kubitzki |author2=H. Huber |author3=P.J. Rudall |author4=P.S. Stevens |year=1998 |publisher=Springer |isbn=3-540-64061-4 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bNQDsSmx2roC&q=Callisia+fragrans&pg=PA115}}{{cite web |title=POTENTIAL ENVIRONMENTAL WEEDS IN AUSTRALIA |url=http://www.weeds.gov.au/publications/books/pubs/potential.pdf |work=NATIONAL WEEDS PROGRAM |publisher=Queensland Department of Natural Resources |access-date=2011-05-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071010044320/http://www.weeds.gov.au/publications/books/pubs/potential.pdf |archive-date=2007-10-10 |url-status=dead }} ==Range and cultivation== ''Callisia fragrans'''is [[endemic]] to [[Mexico]] (from [[Tamaulipas]] to [[Yucatán]]), and naturalized in the [[West Indies]], scattered locations in the [[United States]], and a few other places.[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=223393 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]{{cite web|title=Ecology and Evolutionary Biology Plant Growth Facilities|url=http://titanarum.uconn.edu/198500190.html|publisher=University of Connecticut}} It has been cultivated in many countries as an indoor ornamental since the early 1900s.{{cite journal |last1=Yarmolinsky |first1=Ludmila |last2=Zaccai |first2=Michele |last3=Ben-Shabat |first3=Shimon |last4=Huleihel |first4=Mahmoud |title=Anti-Herpetic Activity of ''Callissia fragrans'' and ''Simmondsia chinensis'' Leaf Extracts In Vitro |journal=The Open Virology Journal |date=4 June 2010 |volume=4 |issue=1 |pages=57–62 |doi= 10.2174/1874357901004010057 |doi-access=free|pmid=20700398 |pmc=2918872}} However, it can be also found growing outdoors in warmer climates in moist, fertile soil. The herb likes partially shaded areas. ==Medicinal properties== It has a rich traditional reputation in Mexico as an [[Antiviral drug|antiviral]] and [[antimicrobial]] plant. In [[Eastern Europe]], its leaves are used for the treatment of various skin diseases, burns and joint disorders. An [[ethanol]] leaf extract ([[tincture]]) has been shown to effectively inhibit the infection of [[Vero cell]]s by [[Herpes simplex virus|HSV-1]], [[Herpes simplex virus 2|HSV-2]] and an [[Aciclovir|ACV]]-resistant strain of the latter, ''[[in vitro]]''. However, the ethanol extract, as opposed to an aquatic extract, was ineffective against [[Varicella zoster virus|VZV]]. Though the ethanol leaf extract had a lower [[Selectivity factor|selectivity]] index (toxicity vs. effectiveness) than [[Aciclovir|ACV]], it was able to inhibit the HSV-2 mutant, and may be less toxic than ACV. Direct interaction with the [[virus]]es, and the blocking of their access to l host cells, seems to be involved. == References == {{Reflist}} == External links == {{Commons category-inline|Callisia fragrans|''Callisia fragrans''}}
